title.zh: 卷一百二十七 列傳第七十七: 姚令言 張光晟 源休 喬琳 張涉 蔣鎮 洪經綸 彭偃
title.en: Volume 127 Biographies 77: Yao Lingyan, Zhang Guangcheng, Yuan Xiu, Qiao Lin, Zhang She, Jiang Zhen, Hong Jinglun, Peng Yan
title.raw: 卷一百二十七 列傳第七十七: 姚令言 張光晟 源休 喬琳 張涉 蔣鎮 洪經綸 彭偃 Volume 127 Biographies 77: Yao Lingyan, Zhang Guangcheng, Yuan Xiu, Qiao Lin, Zhang She, Jiang Zhen, Hong Jinglun, Peng Yan

sentences.zh: 姚令言，河中人也。

translations.literal: Yao Lingyan was a native of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan was from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少應募，起於卒伍，隸涇原節度馬璘。

translations.literal: In his youth he answered the call for recruits, rose from the ranks, and served under Ma Lin, military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he enlisted, rose through the ranks, and served under Ma Lin, military commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 以戰功累授金吾大將軍同正，為衙前兵馬使，改試太常卿、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: For successive battlefield achievements he was promoted to supernumerary Grand General of the Golden Chariots, made Yamen forward military commissioner, and then given provisional appointment as Grand Master of Ceremonies while concurrently serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His battlefield achievements earned him successive promotions to supernumerary Grand General of the Golden Chariots and Yamen forward military commissioner, after which he received provisional appointment as Grand Master of Ceremonies with concurrent duties as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，孟暤為涇原節度留後，自以文吏進身，不樂軍旅，頻表薦令言謹肅，堪任將帥。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Meng Hao served as acting military commissioner of Jingyuan; considering himself a man advanced through civil office, he took no pleasure in military affairs and repeatedly memorialized recommending that Lingyan was conscientious and suited to command troops.
translations.idiomatic: In 780, Meng Hao was acting military commissioner of Jingyuan. A career civil official, he had little taste for military affairs and repeatedly memorialized the throne praising Lingyan as conscientious and fit for field command.

sentences.zh: 暤尋歸朝廷，遂拜令言為四鎮北庭行營涇原節度使、涇州刺史、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long Hao returned to the court, and Lingyan was then appointed military commissioner of Jingyuan for the Four Garrisons and Northern Court campaign force, prefect of Jing Prefecture, and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hao was recalled to the capital, and Lingyan was appointed military commissioner of Jingyuan for the Four Garrisons and Northern Court campaign force, prefect of Jing Prefecture, and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，李希烈叛，寇陷汝州，詔哥舒曜率師攻之，營於襄城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, Li Xilie rebelled, raided and captured Ru Prefecture, and an edict ordered Geshu Yao to lead troops against him and encamp at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In 783, Li Xilie rebelled and seized Ru Prefecture. The court ordered Geshu Yao to lead an army against him and encamp at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 希烈兵數萬圍襄城，勢甚危急。

translations.literal: Xilie's troops, numbering in the tens of thousands, besieged Xiangcheng, and the situation was extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of Xilie's troops besieged Xiangcheng, and the situation grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔令言率本鎮兵五萬赴援。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict ordered Lingyan to lead fifty thousand troops of his circuit to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, the court ordered Lingyan to march fifty thousand men from his circuit to the relief of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 涇師離鎮，多攜子弟而來，望至京師以獲厚賞，及師上路，一無所賜。

translations.literal: When the Jing troops left their garrison, many brought wives and children along, hoping to reach the capital and receive generous rewards; yet once the army was on the road, they received nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing troops left their garrison with many wives and children in tow, expecting rich rewards once they reached the capital, but received nothing once they were on the march.

sentences.zh: 時詔京兆尹王翃犒軍士，唯糲食菜啖而已，軍士覆而不顧，皆憤怒，揚言曰：「吾輩棄父母妻子，將死於難，而食不得飽，安能以草命捍白刃耶！

translations.literal: At that time it was decreed that Wang Hong, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, should reward the troops, but they were given only coarse grain and vegetables to eat; the soldiers overturned the food and ignored it. All were angry and declared aloud: "We have abandoned parents, wives, and children and are about to die in hardship, yet we cannot eat our fill—how can we risk our paltry lives against naked blades!"
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Wang Hong, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, to reward the troops, but they were fed only coarse grain and vegetables. The soldiers overturned the food in disgust. Furious, they cried out: "We have left parents, wives, and children behind to face death, yet we cannot even eat our fill—why should we throw away our worthless lives against cold steel?"

sentences.zh: 國家瓊林、大盈，寶貨堆積，不取此以自活，何往耶？

translations.literal: The state has the Qionlin and Daying treasuries piled high with precious goods—we do not take these to keep ourselves alive; where else shall we go?"
translations.idiomatic: The state keeps the Qionlin and Daying treasuries heaped with treasure. If we will not take from them to save ourselves, where else can we turn?"

sentences.zh: 」行次浐水，乃返戈，大呼鼓噪而還。

translations.literal: When they reached the Chan River, they turned their weapons about, shouting and beating drums as they marched back.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Chan River, they turned their weapons about, shouting and beating drums as they marched back toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 令言曰：「比約東都有厚賞，兒郎勿草草，此非求活之良圖也。

translations.literal: Lingyan said: "We agreed earlier that there would be generous rewards in the eastern capital—men, do not act rashly; this is not a sound plan for survival."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyan said, "We were promised rich rewards in the eastern capital—men, do not act rashly. This is no sound way to save yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」眾不聽，以戈環令言請退，令言急奏之。

translations.literal: The crowd would not listen; they surrounded Lingyan with spears and asked him to withdraw, and he urgently reported the matter to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The men would not listen. They ringed Lingyan with spears and demanded that he step aside, and he urgently reported the mutiny to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上恐，令內庫出繒彩二十車馳賜之，軍聲浩浩，令言不能戢。

translations.literal: The emperor, in fear, ordered twenty cartloads of silk brocade rushed from the inner treasury as gifts, but the army's clamor was vast and Lingyan could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, the emperor ordered twenty cartloads of silk brocade rushed from the inner treasury as gifts, but the troops' uproar only grew louder and Lingyan could not quiet them.

sentences.zh: 街市居人狼狽走竄，亂兵呼曰：「勿走，不稅汝間架矣！

translations.literal: Market dwellers fled in panic, and the mutinous troops shouted: "Do not run—we will not levy the jianjia tax on you!"
translations.idiomatic: People in the streets fled in panic as the mutineers shouted, "Do not run—we will not levy the jianjia tax on you!"

sentences.zh: 」德宗令普王與學士姜公輔往撫勞之，才出內門，賊已斬關，陣於丹鳳樓下。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong ordered the Prince of Pu and Academician Jiang Gongfu to go and comfort them, but they had barely passed the inner gate when the rebels had already broken through the barrier and formed ranks below the Danfeng Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong sent the Prince of Pu and Academician Jiang Gongfu to soothe the troops, but they had barely passed the inner gate when the rebels had already broken through the barrier and drawn up in formation below the Danfeng Tower.

sentences.zh: 是日，德宗倉卒出幸，賊縱入府庫輦運，極力而止。

translations.literal: That day Dezong fled the capital in haste; the rebels were allowed into the treasuries to haul away goods, and only with great effort was this stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That day Dezong fled the capital in haste. The rebels poured into the treasuries to haul away goods, and only with great effort was the looting brought to a halt.

sentences.zh: 時太尉硃泚罷鎮居晉昌裏第，是夜，叛卒謀曰：「硃太尉久囚於宅，若迎為主，大事濟矣。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Preceptor Zhu Ci, having been removed from his command, was living in his residence in Jinchang Lane; that night the mutinous troops plotted: "Grand Preceptor Zhu has long been confined to his house—if we welcome him as our leader, the great affair will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Grand Preceptor Zhu Ci, stripped of his command, was living in his mansion in Jinchang Lane. That night the mutineers plotted: "Grand Preceptor Zhu has been shut up in his house for ages—if we make him our leader, the great enterprise will succeed."

sentences.zh: 」泚嘗節制涇州，眾知其失權，廢居怏怏，又幸泚寬和，乃請令言率騎迎泚於晉昌裏。

translations.literal: Ci had once commanded Jing Prefecture; the troops knew he had lost power and lived in discontented retirement, and they also counted on Ci's mild and generous nature, so they asked Lingyan to lead cavalry to welcome Ci from Jinchang Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Ci had once held command over Jing Prefecture. The men knew he had lost power and brooded in forced retirement, and they also trusted his mild and generous temper, so they asked Lingyan to lead cavalry to fetch him from Jinchang Lane.

sentences.zh: 泚初遲疑，以食飼之，徐觀眾意，既而諸校齊至，乃自第張炬火入居含元殿。

translations.literal: Ci was at first hesitant; they fed him and he slowly gauged the crowd's intent, and when the officers had all assembled he left his residence with torches blazing and took up residence in the Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ci hesitated at first. They fed him while he slowly read the mood of the crowd, and once the officers had all gathered he left his house with torches blazing and took up residence in the Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 既僭號，乃以令言為侍中，與源休同知賊政事。

translations.literal: After he usurped the imperial title, he made Lingyan Palace Attendant and had him administer the rebels' affairs together with Yuan Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: After he usurped the throne, he appointed Lingyan Palace Attendant and had him run rebel affairs jointly with Yuan Xiu.

sentences.zh: 既以身先逆亂，頗盡心於賊，害宗室，圍奉天，皆令言為首帥也。

translations.literal: Since he had personally led the rebellion, he devoted himself thoroughly to the rebels; the slaughter of imperial clansmen and the siege of Fengtian were both led by Lingyan as supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Having personally led the mutiny, he threw himself into the rebel cause. The slaughter of imperial clansmen and the siege of Fengtian were both directed by Lingyan as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 群兇宴樂，既醉，令言與源休論功，令言自此蕭何，源休曰：「帷幄之謀，成秦之業，無出予之右者。

translations.literal: When the rebel leaders feasted and grew drunk, Lingyan and Yuan Xiu disputed their merits; Lingyan claimed he was now the Xiao He of the affair, and Yuan Xiu said: "In stratagems from within the tent and in accomplishing the Qin enterprise, none ranks above me.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast of the rebel leaders, Lingyan and Yuan Xiu, already drunk, began disputing their merits. Lingyan declared himself the Xiao He of the enterprise. Yuan Xiu replied, "In counsel from within the tent and in bringing the Qin enterprise to fruition, none ranks above me.

sentences.zh: 吾比蕭何無讓，子當曹參可矣。

translations.literal: Compared with Xiao He I yield nothing; you may serve as Cao Can."
translations.idiomatic: I yield nothing to Xiao He; you may play Cao Can."

sentences.zh: 」時朝士在賊廷者，聞之皆笑，謂源休為火迫酂侯。

translations.literal: Court officials then present in the rebel court heard this and all laughed, calling Yuan Xiu "the Marquis of Zan, pressed by fire."
translations.idiomatic: Court officials trapped in the rebel court heard this and laughed, dubbing Yuan Xiu "the Marquis of Zan, pressed by fire."

sentences.zh: 硃泚敗，令言與張廷芝尚有眾萬人，從泚將入吐蕃。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci was defeated, Lingyan and Zhang Tingzhi still had a force of ten thousand men and followed Ci intending to enter Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci was defeated, Lingyan and Zhang Tingzhi still commanded ten thousand men and followed Ci toward Tibet.

sentences.zh: 至涇州，欲投田希鑒，希鑒偽致禮誘之，與泚俱斬首來獻。

translations.literal: When they reached Jing Prefecture they wished to submit to Tian Xijian; Xijian feigned courtesy to lure them in, and both they and Ci were beheaded and their heads sent as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At Jing Prefecture they sought refuge with Tian Xijian, who feigned courtesy to lure them in. He beheaded them along with Ci and sent their heads to the court.

sentences.zh: 張光晟，京兆盩厔人，起於行間。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangcheng was a native of Zhouzhi in Jingzhao and rose from the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangcheng was from Zhouzhi in Jingzhao and had risen from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，哥舒翰兵敗潼關，大將王思禮所乘馬中流矢而斃，光晟時在騎卒之中，因下，以馬授思禮。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, Geshu Han's army was defeated at Tong Pass; the horse ridden by the great general Wang Silu was struck by a stray arrow and killed. Guangcheng was then among the cavalrymen; he dismounted and gave his horse to Silu.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianbao era, Geshu Han's army was routed at Tong Pass. The horse of the great general Wang Silu was struck by a stray arrow and killed. Guangcheng, then a cavalryman, dismounted and gave Silu his own mount.

sentences.zh: 思禮問其姓名，不告而退，思禮陰記其形貌，常使人密求之。

translations.literal: Silu asked his name, but he would not tell him and withdrew; Silu secretly noted his appearance and often sent men to search for him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Silu asked his name, but he would not say and slipped away. Silu memorized his face and often sent men to search for him in secret.

sentences.zh: 無何，思禮為河東節度使，其偏將辛雲京為代州刺史，屢為將校譖毀，思禮怒焉。

translations.literal: Before long Silu became military commissioner of Hedong, and his lieutenant Xin Yunjing served as prefect of Dai; he was repeatedly slandered by officers, and Silu grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Silu became military commissioner of Hedong while his lieutenant Xin Yunjing served as prefect of Dai. Officers repeatedly slandered Yunjing, and Silu grew furious.

sentences.zh: 雲京惶懼，不知所出。

translations.literal: Yunjing was fearful and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing was terrified and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 光晟時隸雲京麾下，因間進曰：「光晟素有德於王司空，比不言諸，恥以舊恩受賞。

translations.literal: Guangcheng was then under Yunjing's command and took occasion to advance, saying: "Guangcheng has long owed a debt of gratitude to Minister Wang, but until now I have not spoken of it, ashamed to trade on an old favor for reward.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng then served under Yunjing and seized a private moment to say, "I once did Minister Wang a great service, but I have never spoken of it, ashamed to trade on an old favor for reward.

sentences.zh: 今使君憂迫，光晟請奉命一見司空，則使君之難可解。

translations.literal: Now that my lord is in distress, Guangcheng asks leave to go on your orders and see the minister once—then my lord's difficulty can be resolved."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are in distress, let me go on your orders and see the minister once. Your trouble can then be resolved."

sentences.zh: 」雲京然其計，即令之太原。

translations.literal: Yunjing approved the plan and at once sent him to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yunjing approved the plan and at once sent him to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 乃謁思禮，未及言舊，思禮識之，遽曰：「爾豈非吾故人乎？

translations.literal: He then called on Silu, and before he could speak of the past Silu recognized him and exclaimed: "Are you not my old acquaintance?
translations.idiomatic: He called on Silu, and before he could speak of the past Silu recognized him and cried, "Are you not my old acquaintance?

sentences.zh: 何相見之晚也！

translations.literal: Why have we met so late!"
translations.idiomatic: Why have we met so late!"

sentences.zh: 」光晟遂陳潼關之事，思禮大喜，因執其手感泣曰：「吾有今日，子之力也。

translations.literal: Guangcheng then related the affair at Tong Pass; Silu was greatly pleased, took his hand, and wept, saying: "That I have today is your doing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng then told the story of Tong Pass. Silu was overjoyed, took his hand, and wept. "That I am alive today is your doing.

sentences.zh: 求子頗久，竟此相遇，何慰如之？

translations.literal: I have sought you for a long time, and at last we meet—what comfort could be greater?"
translations.idiomatic: I have searched for you so long, and at last we meet. What comfort could be greater?"

sentences.zh: 」命同榻而坐，結為兄弟。

translations.literal: He ordered them to sit on the same couch and they became sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He had them sit on the same couch and they became sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 光晟遂述雲京之屈，思禮曰：「雲京比涉謗言，過亦不細，今為故人，特舍之矣。

translations.literal: Guangcheng then explained Yunjing's grievance; Silu said: "Yunjing has lately been involved in slander, and his fault is not slight, but for your sake as an old friend I shall specially pardon him."
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng then explained Yunjing's plight. Silu said, "Yunjing has lately been tangled in slander, and his fault is not slight, but for your sake as an old friend I shall pardon him."

sentences.zh: 」即日擢光晟為兵馬使，賚田宅、縑帛甚厚，累奏特進，試太常少卿，委以心腹。

translations.literal: That same day he promoted Guangcheng to military commissioner, bestowed fields, houses, and silk in great abundance, repeatedly memorialized for his extraordinary promotion, gave him provisional appointment as Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and entrusted him as a close confidant.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he promoted Guangcheng to military commissioner, lavished fields, houses, and silk on him, repeatedly memorialized for his extraordinary promotion, gave him provisional appointment as Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and treated him as a trusted confidant.

sentences.zh: 及雲京為河東節度使，又奏光晟為代州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yunjing became military commissioner of Hedong, he again memorialized to make Guangcheng prefect of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunjing became military commissioner of Hedong, he again memorialized to appoint Guangcheng prefect of Dai.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，遷單於都護、兼御史中丞、振武軍使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali era he was transferred to be Protector-General of Chanyu, concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, and commissioner of the Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dali era he was appointed Protector-General of Chanyu with concurrent duties as Vice Censor-in-Chief and commissioner of the Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 代宗密謂之曰：「北蕃縱橫日久，當思所禦之計。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong said to him in secret: "The northern barbarians have run rampant for a long time—you must think of measures to check them."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong told him in private, "The northern tribes have run rampant for years. You must devise a way to hold them in check."

sentences.zh: 」光晟既受命，至鎮，威令甚行。

translations.literal: Once Guangcheng had received his commission and reached his post, his authority and orders were vigorously enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guangcheng took up his post, his authority was swiftly and firmly enforced.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，回紇突董梅錄領眾並雜種胡等自京師還國，輿載金帛，相屬於道。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, the Uyghur Tudun Meilu led his followers together with various other Hu peoples back from the capital to their country, their carts laden with gold and silk in an unbroken line along the road.
translations.idiomatic: In 780, the Uyghur leader Tudun Meilu led his followers and various other Hu peoples homeward from the capital, their carts laden with gold and silk in an unbroken line along the road.

sentences.zh: 光晟訝其裝橐頗多，潛令驛吏以長錐刺之，則皆輦歸所誘致京師婦人也。

translations.literal: Guangcheng was surprised that their baggage was so plentiful and secretly ordered relay clerks to pierce it with long awls; inside were all women they had enticed and brought back from the capital in palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng was struck by how heavy their baggage looked and secretly ordered relay clerks to pierce the loads with long awls. Each pack concealed a woman they had lured from the capital and carried home in a palanquin.

sentences.zh: 遂給突董及所領徒悉令赴宴，酒酣，光晟伏甲盡拘而殺之，死者千余人，唯留二胡歸國復命。

translations.literal: He then invited Tudun and all his followers to a feast; when the wine had gone deep, Guangcheng's hidden soldiers seized and killed them all—more than a thousand dead—and kept only two Hu men to return home and report.
translations.idiomatic: He then invited Tudun and all his followers to a feast. When the wine had gone deep, Guangcheng's hidden soldiers seized and slaughtered them—more than a thousand dead—keeping only two Hu men alive to return home and report.

sentences.zh: 遂部其婦人，給糧還京，收其金帛，賞賚軍士。

translations.literal: He then escorted the women, provided grain for their return to the capital, seized their gold and silk, and rewarded the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He then escorted the women back to the capital with provisions, seized their gold and silk, and distributed the spoils among his troops.

sentences.zh: 後回紇遣使來訴，上不欲甚阻蕃情，征拜右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Later the Uyghurs sent envoys to protest; the emperor, unwilling to alienate the tribes too deeply, summoned him and appointed him General of the Right Golden Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs sent envoys to protest, the emperor, unwilling to estrange the tribes further, recalled him and appointed him General of the Right Golden Chariots.

sentences.zh: 回紇猶怨懟不已，又降為睦王傅，尋改太仆卿，負才怏怏不得誌。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs still nursed their grievance without cease, and he was again demoted to tutor of the Prince of Mu, then changed to Minister of the Stud, resentful in his talent and unable to fulfill his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs still nursed their grievance, and he was demoted again to tutor of the Prince of Mu, then transferred to Minister of the Stud. Talented but thwarted, he brooded over his lost ambitions.

sentences.zh: 賊泚僭逆，署光晟偽節度使兼宰相。

translations.literal: When the rebel Ci usurped power, he appointed Guangcheng false military commissioner and concurrently chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Zhu Ci seized power, he appointed Guangcheng false military commissioner and concurrently chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及泚眾頻敗，遂擇精兵五千配光晟，營於九曲，去東渭橋凡十餘里。

translations.literal: When Ci's forces suffered repeated defeats, he selected five thousand elite troops and assigned them to Guangcheng, who encamped at Jiuqu, a little more than ten li from the Eastern Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: As Ci's forces suffered repeated defeats, he assigned Guangcheng five thousand elite troops and had him encamp at Jiuqu, a little more than ten li from the Eastern Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 光晟潛使於李晟，有歸順之意。

translations.literal: Guangcheng secretly sent envoys to Li Sheng, showing an intention to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng secretly sent envoys to Li Sheng, signaling his wish to defect.

sentences.zh: 晟進兵入苑，光晟勸賊泚宜速西奔，光晟以數千人送泚出城，因率眾回降於晟。

translations.literal: When Sheng advanced into the imperial park, Guangcheng urged the rebel Ci to flee west at once; with several thousand men Guangcheng escorted Ci out of the city, then led his troops back to surrender to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng advanced into the imperial park, Guangcheng urged Ci to flee west at once, escorted him out of the city with several thousand men, and then led his troops back to surrender to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 晟以其誠款，又愛其材，欲奏用之，俾令歸私第，表請特減其罪。

translations.literal: Sheng, because of his sincere submission and also cherishing his talent, wished to memorialize for his employment, had him return to his private residence, and submitted a memorial asking that his crime be specially reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by his sincere submission and his talent, Sheng wished to recommend him for office, sent him to his private residence, and memorialized the throne to reduce his punishment.

sentences.zh: 每大宴會，皆令就坐，華州節度使駱元光詬之曰：「吾不能與反虜同席！

translations.literal: At every great banquet he was made to take a seat, but Luo Yuanguang, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, reviled him, saying: "I cannot sit at the same table with a rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: At every great banquet Sheng seated him with the other commanders, but Luo Yuanguang, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, reviled him, saying, "I will not sit at the same table with a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 」拂衣還營。

translations.literal: He swept his robes and returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: He swept his robes aside and returned to camp.

sentences.zh: 晟不得已，拘之私第，後有詔言其狀跡不可原，乃斬之。

translations.literal: Sheng had no choice but to detain him in his private residence; later an edict declared that his conduct and record could not be pardoned, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had no choice but to confine him to his private residence. Later an edict declared that his conduct could not be pardoned, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 源休，相州臨漳人，京兆尹光輿之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu was a native of Linzhang in Xiang Prefecture and the son of Guangyu, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu was from Linzhang in Xiang Prefecture and was the son of Guangyu, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 休以幹局，累授監察御史、殿中侍御史、青苗使判官，遷虞部員外郎，。

translations.literal: Xiu, for his administrative ability, was repeatedly appointed Investigating Censor, Attending Censor within the Palace, and aide to the Green Sprouts commissioner, then transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Known for his administrative ability, Xiu rose through appointments as Investigating Censor, Attending Censor within the Palace, and aide to the Green Sprouts commissioner, then became Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 出潭州刺史，入為主客郎中，遷給事中、御史中丞、左庶子。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Tan Prefecture, entered the capital as Director of the Bureau of Hosts, and was transferred to Supervising Secretary, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Left Vice Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Tan Prefecture, returned to the capital as Director of the Bureau of Hosts, and was promoted to Supervising Secretary, Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Left Vice Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 其妻即吏部侍郎王翊女也。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of Wang Yi, Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the daughter of Wang Yi, Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 因小忿而離，妻族上訴，下御史臺驗理，休遲留不答款狀，除名，配流溱州。

translations.literal: Because of a minor quarrel they separated; his wife's kin appealed upward, and the case was sent down to the Censorate for investigation. Xiu delayed and would not answer the written interrogatory; he was struck from the rolls and exiled to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a minor quarrel they separated. His wife's kin appealed to the authorities, and the Censorate was ordered to investigate. Xiu stalled and refused to answer the written interrogatory, was struck from the rolls, and exiled to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，移岳州。

translations.literal: After a long while he was moved to Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was transferred to Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建中初，楊炎執政，以京兆尹嚴郢威名稍著，心欲傾之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Yang Yan held power; Yan Ying, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, was gaining a reputation, and Yan wished to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianzhong era, Yang Yan held power. Yan Ying, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, was growing in reputation, and Yang Yan wished to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 郢，即王翊甥婿也。

translations.literal: Ying was the nephew by marriage of Wang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was Wang Yi's nephew by marriage.

sentences.zh: 休與王氏離絕之時，炎風聞休、郢有隙，遂擢休自流人為京兆少尹，俾令伺郢過失。

translations.literal: When Xiu had broken with the Wang clan, Yan heard that Xiu and Ying were at odds and therefore promoted Xiu from exile to be Vice Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, ordering him to watch for Ying's faults.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu had broken with the Wang clan, Yang Yan heard that Xiu and Ying were at odds and promoted Xiu from exile to Vice Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, ordering him to watch for Ying's faults.

sentences.zh: 休既職久，與郢親善，炎怒之，奏令以本官兼御史中丞，奉使回紇。

translations.literal: After Xiu had long held office he grew friendly with Ying, and Yan was angry; he memorialized that Xiu should retain his post while concurrently serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief and be sent on embassy to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu had been in office for some time he grew friendly with Ying, enraging Yang Yan, who memorialized that Xiu should retain his post while concurrently serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief and be sent on embassy to the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 休至振武，軍使張光晟已殺回紇突董等，上初欲遂絕其使，令休還，待命於太原。

translations.literal: When Xiu reached Zhenwu, the army commissioner Zhang Guangcheng had already killed the Uyghur Tudun and others; the emperor at first wished to break off relations entirely and ordered Xiu to return, awaiting orders at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu reached Zhenwu, army commissioner Zhang Guangcheng had already killed Tudun and the other Uyghur leaders. The emperor at first wished to break off relations entirely and ordered Xiu back to await further orders at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 久之方遣，仍令休歸其突董、翳密施大小梅錄等四屍。

translations.literal: Only after a long delay was he sent forth, and Xiu was still ordered to return the four corpses of Tudun, Yimishi, and the great and small Meilu.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long delay was he sent forth, still charged with returning the four corpses of Tudun, Yimishi, and the great and small Meilu.

sentences.zh: 突董者，即武義可汗之叔父也。

translations.literal: Tudun was the uncle of the Wuyi Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Tudun was the uncle of the Wuyi Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 屍既至，可汗令宰臣已下具彩服車馬來迎。

translations.literal: When the corpses arrived, the qaghan ordered his ministers and all below to come out in colored robes with carriages and horses to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When the corpses arrived, the qaghan ordered his ministers and officials to come out in colored robes with carriages and horses to receive them.

sentences.zh: 其宰相頡於思迦坐大帳，立休等於帳外雪中，詰殺突董等故。

translations.literal: His chancellor Xieyusijia sat in the great tent and had Xiu and the others stand in the snow outside the tent, questioning them on the reason for killing Tudun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor Xieyusijia sat in the great tent and had Xiu and his party stand in the snow outside, demanding to know why Tudun and the others had been killed.

sentences.zh: 休曰：「突董等自與張光晟忿鬥而死，非天子命也。

translations.literal: Xiu said: "Tudun and the others died in a quarrel with Zhang Guangcheng of their own accord—it was not by the Son of Heaven's command."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu said, "Tudun and the others died in a quarrel with Zhang Guangcheng of their own accord. It was not by the Son of Heaven's command."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「使者背唐國，負罪當死，不能自戮耶？

translations.literal: They asked again: "The envoy has turned against Tang and bears a crime deserving death—cannot he kill himself?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "The envoy has turned against Tang and bears a crime deserving death. Cannot he kill himself?"

sentences.zh: 不然，何假手於我殺之也？

translations.literal: If not, why borrow our hands to kill him?"
translations.idiomatic: If not, why borrow our hands to kill him?"

sentences.zh: 」凡將殺者數矣，言頗悖慢，乃引去，供餼甚薄，留之五十余日，乃得還。

translations.literal: Several times they were on the point of killing him; his words were quite insolent. They then led him away, provided very meager provisions, detained him for more than fifty days, and only then allowed him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Several times they were on the point of killing him, and his replies were openly insolent. They led him away, provided meager provisions, and detained him for more than fifty days before allowing him to return.

sentences.zh: 可汗使謂休曰：「我國人皆欲殺汝，唯我不然。

translations.literal: The qaghan's envoy said to Xiu: "All my people wish to kill you, but I alone do not."
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan's envoy told Xiu, "All my people wish to kill you, but I alone do not."

sentences.zh: 汝國已殺突董等，吾又殺汝，猶以血洗血，汙益甚爾。

translations.literal: Your state has already killed Tudun and the others; if I kill you too, it is still washing blood with blood, and the stain grows only worse.
translations.idiomatic: Your state has already killed Tudun and the others. If I kill you too, it is still washing blood with blood, and the stain only grows worse.

sentences.zh: 吾今以水洗血，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: I now wash blood with water—is that not better!"
translations.idiomatic: I now wash blood with water. Is that not better?"

sentences.zh: 所欠吾馬直絹一百八十萬疋，當速歸之。

translations.literal: The one million eight hundred thousand bolts of silk owed for our horses' price must be returned at once."
translations.idiomatic: The one million eight hundred thousand bolts of silk still owed for our horses must be returned at once."

sentences.zh: 」遣散支將軍康赤心等隨休來朝，休竟不得見其可汗。

translations.literal: He sent the general Kang Chixin and others to accompany Xiu on his return to court, but Xiu never obtained an audience with the qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Kang Chixin and others to accompany Xiu back to court, but Xiu never obtained an audience with the qaghan.

sentences.zh: 尋遣赤心等歸，與之帛十萬疋、金銀十萬兩，償其馬直。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Chixin and the others were sent back, and they were given one hundred thousand bolts of silk and one hundred thousand taels of gold and silver to pay the horse price.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Chixin and his party were sent back with one hundred thousand bolts of silk and one hundred thousand taels of gold and silver to settle the horse debt.

sentences.zh: 休履危而還，宰相盧杞又恐復命之日以口辯結恩，將至太原，遽奏為光祿卿。

translations.literal: Xiu returned after passing through danger; Chancellor Lu Qi again feared that on the day of his report he would win favor through eloquence, and when he was about to reach Taiyuan Qi urgently memorialized to make him Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu returned after a perilous mission. Chancellor Lu Qi feared that on reporting back he would win favor through eloquence, and when Xiu was nearing Taiyuan, Qi urgently memorialized to appoint him Minister of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 休以其還使賞薄，居常怨望。

translations.literal: Xiu, because the rewards for his return mission were meager, constantly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu felt the rewards for his embassy were meager and constantly nursed his resentment.

sentences.zh: 會涇原兵叛，立硃泚為主。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jingyuan troops rebelled and set up Zhu Ci as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingyuan troops rebelled, they set up Zhu Ci as their leader.

sentences.zh: 初但稱太尉，朝官謁泚者，悉勸奏迎鑾駕，既不合泚意而退。

translations.literal: At first he was called only Grand Preceptor; court officials who visited Ci all urged memorializing to welcome back the imperial carriage, but this did not suit Ci's intent and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ci was addressed only as Grand Preceptor. Court officials who visited him urged memorializing to welcome back the emperor, but when this did not suit Ci's intent they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及休至，遂屏人移時，言多悖逆，盛陳成敗，稱述符命，勸令僭號。

translations.literal: When Xiu arrived, they dismissed attendants and talked for a long while; his words were largely rebellious, he set forth success and failure at length, cited portents and mandates, and urged usurpation of the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu arrived, they dismissed attendants and talked at length. His words were openly rebellious. He laid out success and failure at length, cited portents and mandates, and urged Ci to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 泚悅其言，以休為宰相，判度支。

translations.literal: Ci was pleased with his words and made Xiu chancellor with charge over the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Ci was pleased with his counsel and made Xiu chancellor with charge over the treasury.

sentences.zh: 休遂為謀主，至於兵食軍資，遷除補擬，內外咨謀，一稟休畫。

translations.literal: Xiu then became chief strategist; as to troops, provisions, military supplies, appointments and replacements, and counsel within and without, all followed Xiu's plans alone.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu then became chief strategist. Troops, provisions, military supplies, appointments, and counsel within and without all followed his plans alone.

sentences.zh: 故時人云：「源休之逆，甚於硃泚。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time said: "Yuan Xiu's rebellion is worse than Zhu Ci's."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said, "Yuan Xiu's treason was worse than Zhu Ci's."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷大臣之奔竄不獲者，多為休所誘致，以至戮辱，職休而為，蓋非一焉。

translations.literal: Court grandees who fled but could not escape were mostly lured in by Xiu, leading to slaughter and humiliation; deeds done at Xiu's instigation were by no means few.
translations.idiomatic: Court grandees who fled but could not escape were mostly lured in by Xiu to slaughter and humiliation. Deeds done at his instigation were by no means few.

sentences.zh: 又勸泚鋤翦宗室，以絕人望，命萬年縣賊曹尉楊偡專其斷決，諸王子孫遇害不可勝數。

translations.literal: He also urged Ci to root out the imperial clan to cut off popular hopes, appointed Yang Yan of Wannian County, clerk of the bandit-catchers bureau, to decide cases exclusively, and princes and their descendants who suffered could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged Ci to root out the imperial clan to cut off popular hopes, appointed Yang Yan of Wannian County, clerk of the bandit-catchers bureau, to decide such cases exclusively, and princes and their descendants fell victim beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 泚敗走，休隨至寧州。

translations.literal: When Ci was defeated and fled, Xiu followed him to Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Ci was defeated and fled, Xiu followed him to Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 泚死，休走鳳翔，為其部曲所殺，傳首來獻。

translations.literal: When Ci died, Xiu fled to Fengxiang and was killed by his own troops; his head was sent in as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After Ci died, Xiu fled to Fengxiang, where his own troops killed him and sent his head to the court.

sentences.zh: 休三子並斬於東市，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Xiu's three sons were all beheaded at the eastern market, and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's three sons were beheaded at the eastern market, and his household goods were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 喬琳，太原人。

translations.literal: Qiao Lin was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Lin was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧誌學，以文詞稱。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, he was resolved to study and was famed for literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a youth, he devoted himself to study and won renown for his literary skill.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，舉進士，補成武尉，累授興平尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed defender of Chengwu, and was repeatedly promoted to defender of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination, served as defender of Chengwu, and was repeatedly promoted to defender of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 朔方節度郭子儀辟為掌書記，尋拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, recruited him as chief secretary, and he was soon appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, military commissioner of Shuofang, recruited him as chief secretary, and he was soon appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 琳倜儻疏誕，好談諧，侮謔僚列，頗無禮檢。

translations.literal: Lin was unconventional and unrestrained, fond of wit and banter, mocking and jesting at his colleagues, and quite without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was unconventional and unrestrained, fond of wit and banter, and mocked his colleagues with little regard for propriety.

sentences.zh: 同院御史畢耀初與琳嘲誚往復，因成釁隙，遂以公事互相告訴，坐貶巴州員外司戶。

translations.literal: Bi Yao, a censor of the same bureau, at first exchanged mockery with Lin back and forth, which bred a feud; they then accused each other on official business and were demoted to supernumerary registrar of Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yao, a censor of the same bureau, at first traded mockery with Lin until a feud developed. They then accused each other on official business and were demoted to supernumerary registrar of Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遂起為南郭令，改殿中侍御史，充山南節度張獻誠行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was then raised up as magistrate of the southern suburb, changed to Attending Censor within the Palace, and served as campaign military aide to Zhang Xiancheng, military commissioner of Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed magistrate of the southern suburb, promoted to Attending Censor within the Palace, and served as campaign military aide to Zhang Xiancheng, military commissioner of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 使罷，為劍南東川節度鮮于叔明判官。

translations.literal: When the mission ended, he became aide to Xianyu Shuming, military commissioner of eastern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission ended, he became aide to Xianyu Shuming, military commissioner of eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 改檢校駕部郎中、果綿遂三州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Supernumerary Director of the Bureau of the Imperial Stud, concurrently prefect of Guo, Mian, and Su prefectures, and Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supernumerary Director of the Bureau of the Imperial Stud with concurrent posts as prefect of Guo, Mian, and Su prefectures and as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 入為大理少卿、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of Justice and Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Vice Minister of Justice and Rector of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 出為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 琳素與張涉友善，上在春宮，涉嘗為侍讀。

translations.literal: Lin had long been friendly with Zhang She; when the emperor was crown prince, She had once served as his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had long been friendly with Zhang She, who had served as the crown prince's tutor.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，多以政事詢訪於涉，盛稱琳識度材略，堪備大用，因拜御史大夫、平章事。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne he often consulted She on state affairs; She greatly praised Lin's judgment and talent as fit for great employment, and Lin was therefore appointed Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: After he succeeded to the throne, he often consulted She on state affairs. She praised Lin's judgment and talent as fit for high office, and Lin was appointed Censor-in-Chief and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 琳本粗材，又年高有耳疾，上每顧問，對答失次，論奏不合時。

translations.literal: Lin was by nature coarse material, and moreover was advanced in years and hard of hearing; whenever the emperor questioned him his answers were disorderly and his memorials ill suited to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was a coarse man by nature, and he was elderly and hard of hearing. Whenever the emperor questioned him, his answers were disorderly and his memorials ill suited to the times.

sentences.zh: 幸居相位凡八十余日，除工部尚書，罷知政事，尋加迎皇太后副使。

translations.literal: Fortunately he held the chancellorship for only a little more than eighty days before being made Minister of Works and removed from governing affairs; soon afterward he was additionally made deputy envoy to welcome the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He held the chancellorship for only a little more than eighty days before being made Minister of Works and removed from governing affairs. Soon afterward he was additionally appointed deputy envoy to welcome the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之亂，扈從至奉天，轉吏部尚書，遷太子少師。

translations.literal: During Zhu Ci's rebellion he followed the emperor to Fengtian, was transferred to Minister of Personnel, and promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion he followed the emperor to Fengtian, was transferred to Minister of Personnel, and promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 再幸梁、洋，從至盩厔，托以馬乏遲留，上以琳舊老，心敬重之，慰諭頗至，以禦馬一匹給焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor again visited Liang and Yang, Lin followed as far as Zhouzhi and pleaded that his horses were exhausted and he must delay; because Lin was old and venerable the emperor respected him in his heart, comforted him at length, and gave him an imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor again visited Liang and Yang, Lin followed as far as Zhouzhi and pleaded exhaustion of his horses. The emperor, respecting his age, comforted him at length and gave him an imperial mount.

sentences.zh: 又懇辭以老疾不堪山阻登頓，上悵然，賜之所執策曰：「勉為良圖，與卿決矣。

translations.literal: He again begged off, saying his old illness made him unable to endure mountain barriers and steep climbs; the emperor was sorrowful and gave him the whip he held, saying: "Strive for a sound plan—I have parted with you."
translations.idiomatic: He again begged off, saying his old illness made him unable to endure mountain barriers and steep climbs. The emperor was sorrowful and gave him the whip he held, saying, "Strive for a sound plan. I have parted with you."

sentences.zh: 」後數日，乃削發為僧，止仙遊寺。

translations.literal: A few days later he shaved his head and became a monk, residing at Xianyou Temple.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he shaved his head and became a monk at Xianyou Temple.

sentences.zh: 賊泚聞之，遂令數十騎追至京城，俾為偽吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the rebel Ci heard of this, he sent several dozen horsemen to pursue him to the capital and made him false Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Zhu Ci heard of this, he sent several dozen horsemen to pursue him to the capital and made him false Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 令源休被公服，饋肉食，琳雖辭讓，而僧言求施。

translations.literal: He had Yuan Xiu clothe him in official robes and present meat food; though Lin declined, the monk's words were those of one begging alms.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yuan Xiu clothe him in official robes and present meat, but though Lin declined, his words sounded like those of a monk begging alms.

sentences.zh: 琳掌賊中吏部，選人前請曰：「所註某官不穩便。

translations.literal: Lin managed the rebels' Ministry of Personnel; a candidate came forward and said: "The office you have assigned me is not secure."
translations.idiomatic: Lin managed the rebels' Ministry of Personnel. A candidate came forward and said, "The office you have assigned me is not secure."

sentences.zh: 」琳謂之曰：「足下謂此選竟穩便乎？

translations.literal: Lin said to him: "Do you suppose this appointment is secure after all?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin replied, "Do you suppose this appointment is secure after all?"

sentences.zh: 」及官軍收京師，當處極刑，時琳已七十余，李晟憫其衰老，表請減死。

translations.literal: When the imperial army recovered the capital he was due for the extreme penalty; Lin was then already more than seventy, and Li Sheng pitied his old age and memorialized to reduce the sentence from death.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army recovered the capital, he faced the death penalty. Lin was already more than seventy, and Li Sheng pitied his age and memorialized to spare his life.

sentences.zh: 上以其累經重任，頓虧臣節，自受逆命，頗聞譏諧悖慢之言，背義負恩，固不可舍，命斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he had repeatedly held weighty posts yet suddenly lost his ministerial integrity, had himself accepted rebel commands, and was widely reported to have spoken in mockery, insolence, and disrespect, betraying righteousness and failing in gratitude, could by no means be spared, and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Lin, having repeatedly held weighty posts, had suddenly lost his ministerial integrity, accepted rebel commands, and was widely reported to have spoken with mockery and insolence. Having betrayed righteousness and failed in gratitude, he could not be spared, and the emperor ordered him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 臨刑嘆曰：「喬琳以七月七日生，亦以此日死，豈非命歟！」

translations.literal: Facing execution he sighed: "Qiao Lin was born on the seventh day of the seventh month and dies on this day as well—is this not fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution he sighed, "Qiao Lin was born on the seventh day of the seventh month and dies on this day as well. Is this not fate!"

sentences.zh: 張涉者，蒲州人，家世儒者。

translations.literal: Zhang She was a native of Pu Prefecture, from a family of Confucian scholars for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang She was from Pu Prefecture, from a long line of Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 涉依國學為諸生講說，稍遷國子博士，亦能為文，嘗請有司日試萬言，時呼張萬言。

translations.literal: She relied on the National University to lecture students, was gradually promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University, and could also write; he once asked the authorities for a daily examination of ten thousand words, and at the time was called Zhang Ten Thousand Words.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured students at the National University, rose to Erudite of the Imperial University, and was also a capable writer. He once asked the authorities to test him at ten thousand words a day, and people called him Zhang Ten Thousand Words.

sentences.zh: 德宗在春宮，受經於涉。

translations.literal: When Dezong was crown prince, he received the classics from She.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was crown prince, he studied the classics under She.

sentences.zh: 及即位之夕，召涉入宮，訪以庶政，大小之事皆咨之。

translations.literal: On the night he took the throne he summoned She into the palace, consulted him on general administration, and sought his advice on matters great and small.
translations.idiomatic: On the night he took the throne, he summoned She to the palace and consulted him on all matters of government, great and small.

sentences.zh: 翌日，詔居翰林，恩禮甚厚，親重莫比。

translations.literal: The next day an edict placed him in the Hanlin Academy; favor and ceremony were very generous, and none was more intimate or esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict placed him in the Hanlin Academy with lavish favor and ceremony; none was more intimate or esteemed.

sentences.zh: 自博士遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: From Erudite he was transferred to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted from Erudite to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 上方屬意宰輔，唯賢是擇，故求人於不次之地。

translations.literal: The emperor was then intent on chancellors and sought only the worthy, and therefore looked for men in extraordinary places.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then intent on finding worthy chancellors and looked for talent in extraordinary places.

sentences.zh: 涉舉懷州刺史喬琳為相，上授之不疑，天下聞之者皆愕然。

translations.literal: She recommended Qiao Lin, prefect of Huai Prefecture, as chancellor; the emperor appointed him without doubt, and all who heard of it in the realm were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: She recommended Qiao Lin, prefect of Huai Prefecture, as chancellor. The emperor appointed him without hesitation, and all who heard of it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 數月，琳以不稱職罷，上由是疏涉。

translations.literal: After several months Lin was removed for incompetence, and from this the emperor grew distant from She.
translations.idiomatic: After several months Lin was removed for incompetence, and the emperor grew distant from She.

sentences.zh: 俄受前湖南都團練使辛京杲贓事發，詔曰：「尊師之道，禮有所加；

translations.literal: Soon the bribery case of the former regional commander of Hunan, Xin Jinggao, came to light, and an edict said: "In honoring one's teacher, ritual adds something;
translations.idiomatic: Soon the bribery case of the former regional commander of Hunan, Xin Jinggao, came to light. An edict said, "In honoring one's teacher, ritual adds something;

sentences.zh: 議故之法，恩有所掩。

translations.literal: in discussing the law concerning old ties, grace covers something.
translations.idiomatic: in discussing the law concerning old ties, grace may cover something.

sentences.zh: 張涉賄賂交通，頗駭時聽，常所親重，良深嘆惜。

translations.literal: Zhang She's bribery and illicit dealings greatly shocked contemporary opinion; one whom he had long favored and esteemed, and the regret was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang She's bribery and illicit dealings greatly shocked public opinion. He had long been a man the emperor favored and esteemed, and the regret ran very deep.

sentences.zh: 宜放歸田裏。」

translations.literal: He should be released to return to his fields."
translations.idiomatic: He should be released to return to his fields."

sentences.zh: 蔣鎮，常州義興人，尚書左丞洌之子也。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhen was a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture and the son of Jiang Lie, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhen was from Yixing in Chang Prefecture and was the son of Jiang Lie, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 與兄練並以文學進。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Lian both advanced through literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Lian both advanced through literary learning.

sentences.zh: 天寶末舉賢良，累授左拾遺、司封員外郎，轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was recommended as worthy and good, was repeatedly appointed Left Reminder, Vice Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments, and transferred to Remonstrating Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianbao era he was recommended as worthy and good, rose through appointments as Left Reminder and Vice Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments, and was transferred to Remonstrating Councilor.

sentences.zh: 時戶部侍郎、判度支韓滉上言：「河中鹽池生瑞鹽，實土德之上瑞。

translations.literal: At that time Han Huang, Vice Minister of Revenue with charge over the treasury, memorialized: "The salt ponds of Hezhong have produced auspicious salt—truly a supreme omen of the virtue of Earth."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Han Huang, Vice Minister of Revenue with charge over the treasury, memorialized, "The salt ponds of Hezhong have produced auspicious salt—a supreme omen of the virtue of Earth."

sentences.zh: 」上以秋霖稍多，水潦為患，不宜生瑞，命鎮馳驛檢行之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because autumn rains had been rather heavy and flooding was a calamity, held that it was not fitting for omens to appear and ordered Zhen to go by express relay and inspect the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because autumn rains had been heavy and flooding was widespread, held that such omens were ill timed and ordered Zhen to inspect the matter by express relay.

sentences.zh: 鎮奏與滉同，仍上表賀，請宣付史館，並請置神祠，錫其嘉號寶應靈慶池。

translations.literal: Zhen memorialized in agreement with Huang, also submitted a congratulatory memorial, asked that it be proclaimed and sent to the Historiography Office, and requested the establishment of a spirit shrine, bestowing the honorable name Precious Response Spirit Celebration Pond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen reported in agreement with Huang, submitted a congratulatory memorial, asked that the matter be proclaimed and sent to the Historiography Office, and requested a spirit shrine with the honorable name Precious Response Spirit Celebration Pond.

sentences.zh: 地霖潦彌月，壞居人廬舍非一，鹽池為潦水所入，其味多苦。

translations.literal: Rain and flooding lasted a full month, destroying many dwellings of the inhabitants; the salt ponds were entered by floodwater and their taste was largely bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Rain and flooding lasted a full month, destroying many dwellings. Floodwater entered the salt ponds and made the salt largely bitter.

sentences.zh: 韓滉慮鹽戶減稅，詐奏雨不壞池，池生瑞鹽，鎮庇之飾詐，識者醜之。

translations.literal: Han Huang, fearing reduced tax from salt households, falsely memorialized that rain had not harmed the ponds and that the ponds had produced auspicious salt; Zhen shielded him and embellished the fraud, and those who knew were ashamed of them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang, fearing reduced tax from salt households, falsely memorialized that rain had not harmed the ponds and that auspicious salt had appeared. Zhen shielded him and embellished the fraud, and those who knew were ashamed of them.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中、工部侍郎，以簡儉稱於時。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary and Vice Minister of Works and was famed at the time for simplicity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary and Vice Minister of Works and was famed for simplicity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 其妹婿源溥，即休之弟也，以姻媾之故，與休交好。

translations.literal: His sister's husband Yuan Pu was Xiu's younger brother; because of the marriage tie, Zhen was friendly with Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: His sister's husband Yuan Pu was Xiu's younger brother. Through the marriage tie, Zhen was friendly with Xiu.

sentences.zh: 涇師之叛，鎮潛竄，夜至鄠縣西，馬躓墮溝澗中，傷足不能進。

translations.literal: When the Jing troops rebelled, Zhen fled in secret; by night he reached the west of Hu County, his horse stumbled and fell into a ditch, injuring his foot so he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing troops rebelled, Zhen fled in secret. By night he reached the west of Hu County, where his horse stumbled into a ditch and injured his foot so he could not go on.

sentences.zh: 時史練已與源休相率受賊偽官。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Lian had already followed Yuan Xiu in accepting false offices from the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shi Lian had already followed Yuan Xiu in accepting false offices from the rebels.

sentences.zh: 鎮仆人有逃歸投練，雲鎮病足在鄠。

translations.literal: One of Zhen's servants escaped and returned to Lian, reporting that Zhen's injured foot was at Hu.
translations.idiomatic: One of Zhen's servants escaped to Lian and reported that Zhen lay injured at Hu.

sentences.zh: 練與源休聞之大喜，遂言於賊泚此。

translations.literal: Lian and Yuan Xiu were greatly pleased when they heard this and therefore told the rebel Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Lian and Yuan Xiu were greatly pleased when they heard this and told the rebel Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 泚素慕鎮清名，即令騎二百求之鄠縣西。

translations.literal: Ci had long admired Zhen's pure reputation and at once sent two hundred horsemen to seek him west of Hu County.
translations.idiomatic: Ci had long admired Zhen's reputation and at once sent two hundred horsemen to seek him west of Hu County.

sentences.zh: 明日，擁鎮而至，署為偽宰相。

translations.literal: The next day they brought Zhen in with an escort and appointed him false chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they brought Zhen in under escort and appointed him false chancellor.

sentences.zh: 既知不免，每憂沮，常懷刃將自裁，多為兄練所救而罷。

translations.literal: Once he knew he could not escape, he was constantly dejected; he often kept a blade intending to kill himself, but was mostly stopped by his elder brother Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Once he knew he could not escape, he was constantly dejected and often kept a blade intending to kill himself, but was mostly stopped by his elder brother Lian.

sentences.zh: 數日後，復謀竄匿，竟以性懦畏怯，計終不果。

translations.literal: Several days later he again plotted to flee and hide, but in the end, because his nature was timid and fearful, the plan never came to fruition.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he again plotted to flee and hide, but in the end his timid nature kept the plan from coming to fruition.

sentences.zh: 然源休與泚頻議，欲逼脅潛藏衣冠，大加殺戮，鎮輒力爭救，獲全者甚眾。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan Xiu and Ci often discussed forcing out gentry and officials in hiding and slaughtering them on a great scale; Zhen repeatedly strove to save them, and very many were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuan Xiu and Ci often discussed forcing out hidden gentry and officials for slaughter on a great scale. Zhen repeatedly strove to save them, and very many were preserved.

sentences.zh: 至是，與兄練等並授偽職，斬於東市西北街。

translations.literal: At this time he, together with his elder brother Lian and others who had all accepted false offices, was beheaded at the northwest street of the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he, together with his elder brother Lian and others who had accepted false offices, was beheaded at the northwest street of the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 初鎮父洌，叔渙，當祿山、思明之亂，並授偽職，然以家風修整，為士大夫所稱。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhen's father Lie and his uncle Huan, during the rebellions of Lushan and Siming, had both accepted false offices, yet because the family style was cultivated and proper they were praised by scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhen's father Lie and his uncle Huan had accepted false offices during the rebellions of Lushan and Siming, yet because the family style was cultivated and proper they were praised by scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 鎮兄弟亦以教義禮法為己任，而貪祿愛死，節隳身戮，為天下笑。

translations.literal: The Zhen brothers also took instruction in righteousness and ritual law as their charge, yet they clung to salary and loved life, their integrity destroyed and their persons executed, and became the laughingstock of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhen brothers also took instruction in righteousness and ritual law as their charge, yet they clung to salary, loved life, destroyed their integrity, and were executed, becoming the laughingstock of the realm.

sentences.zh: 洪經綸，建中初為黜陟使。

translations.literal: Hong Jinglun served at the beginning of Jianzhong as promotion-and-demotion commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Jinglun served early in the Jianzhong era as promotion-and-demotion commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至東都，訪聞魏州田悅食糧兵凡七萬人，經綸素昧時機，先以符停其兵四萬人，令歸農畝。

translations.literal: When he reached the eastern capital he learned on inquiry that Tian Yue of We Prefecture had grain-paid troops numbering seventy thousand in all; Jinglun, who had never understood the times, first issued a warrant disbanding forty thousand of his troops and ordering them back to the fields.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the eastern capital he learned that Tian Yue of We Prefecture maintained seventy thousand grain-paid troops. Jinglun, who had never understood the times, first issued a warrant disbanding forty thousand of them and ordering them back to the fields.

sentences.zh: 田悅偽順命，即依符罷之；

translations.literal: Tian Yue falsely obeyed the command and at once dismissed them according to the warrant;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue pretended to obey and at once dismissed them according to the warrant;

sentences.zh: 而大集所罷兵士，激怒之曰：「爾等在軍旅，各有父母妻子，既為黜陟使所罷，如何得衣食？

translations.literal: but then gathered the dismissed soldiers in great numbers and incited them, saying: "You are in the army, each with parents, wives, and children; now that the promotion-and-demotion commissioner has dismissed you, how will you obtain food and clothing?"
translations.idiomatic: but then gathered the dismissed soldiers and incited them, saying, "You are in the army, each with parents, wives, and children. Now that the promotion-and-demotion commissioner has dismissed you, how will you obtain food and clothing?"

sentences.zh: 」遂大哭。

translations.literal: They then wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: They then wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 悅乃盡出家財衣服厚給之，各令還其部伍，自此人堅叛心，由是罷職。

translations.literal: Yue then brought out all his household wealth and clothing and gave them generously, ordering each back to his unit; from this the men's resolve to rebel was firm, and Jinglun was removed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then brought out all his household wealth and clothing and gave them generously, ordering each man back to his unit. From this their resolve to rebel was firm, and Jinglun was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 及硃泚反，偽授太常少卿。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he was falsely appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he was falsely appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 彭偃，少負俊才，銳於進取，為當塗者所抑，形於言色。

translations.literal: Peng Yan in youth possessed outstanding talent and was keen to advance, but was suppressed by those in power, which showed in his words and expression.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yan possessed outstanding talent in youth and was keen to advance, but those in power suppressed him, and it showed in his words and expression.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，為都官員外郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali he was Vice Director of the Bureau of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Dali era he was Vice Director of the Bureau of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時劍南東川觀察使李叔明上言，以「佛、道二教，無益於時，請粗加澄汰。

translations.literal: At that time Li Shuming, observation commissioner of eastern Sichuan, memorialized that "the two teachings of Buddhism and Daoism are of no benefit to the age and should be roughly clarified and reduced.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Shuming, observation commissioner of eastern Sichuan, memorialized that "the two teachings of Buddhism and Daoism are of no benefit to the age and should be roughly clarified and reduced.

sentences.zh: 其東川寺觀，請定為二等：上寺留僧二十一人；

translations.literal: For monasteries and abbeys in eastern Sichuan, let them be fixed in two grades: upper monasteries are to retain twenty-one monks;
translations.idiomatic: For monasteries and abbeys in eastern Sichuan, let them be fixed in two grades: upper monasteries are to retain twenty-one monks;

sentences.zh: 上觀留道士十四人，降殺以七，皆精選有道行者，余悉令返初。

translations.literal: upper abbeys fourteen Daoist priests; lower ones seven—all to be carefully selected for those who practice the Way, and the rest all ordered to return to lay life.
translations.idiomatic: upper abbeys fourteen Daoist priests; lower ones seven—all carefully selected for those who practice the Way, and the rest ordered to return to lay life.

sentences.zh: 蘭若、道場無名者皆廢。

translations.literal: Buddhist shrines and ritual sites without established names are all to be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist shrines and ritual sites without established names are all to be abolished."

sentences.zh: 」德宗曰：「叔明此奏，可為天下通制，不唯劍南一道。

translations.literal: Dezong said: "Shuming's memorial may serve as a general regulation for the realm, not only for the Sichuan circuit alone."
translations.idiomatic: Dezong said, "Shuming's memorial may serve as a general regulation for the realm, not only for the Sichuan circuit alone."

sentences.zh: 」下尚書集議。

translations.literal: It was sent down to the Department of State Affairs for collective deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: It was sent down to the Department of State Affairs for collective deliberation.

sentences.zh: 偃獻議曰：

translations.literal: Yan submitted a proposal, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yan submitted a proposal, saying:

sentences.zh: 王者之政，變人心為上，因人心次之，不變不因，循常守固者為下。

translations.literal: In the government of a true king, transforming people's hearts is highest, following people's hearts next, neither transforming nor following is lower, and clinging to the routine and holding fast to the old is lowest.
translations.idiomatic: In the government of a true king, transforming people's hearts is highest, following people's hearts comes next, neither transforming nor following ranks lower, and clinging to routine ranks lowest.

sentences.zh: 故非有獨見之明，不能行非常之事。

translations.literal: Therefore without vision that sees alone, one cannot carry out extraordinary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Without singular vision, one cannot carry out extraordinary affairs.

sentences.zh: 今陛下以惟新之政，為萬代法，若不革舊風，令歸正道者，非也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty, with renewing government as the law for ten thousand generations, would be wrong not to reform old customs and bring them back to the correct path.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty, with renewing government as the law for ten thousand generations, would be wrong not to reform old customs and bring them back to the correct path.

sentences.zh: 當今道士，有名無實，時俗鮮重，亂政猶輕。

translations.literal: Today's Daoist priests have name without substance; the age scarcely esteems them, and their disordering of government is still slight.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Daoist priests have name without substance. The age scarcely esteems them, and their disordering of government is still slight.

sentences.zh: 唯有僧尼，頗為穢雜。

translations.literal: Only monks and nuns are quite impure and mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Only monks and nuns are quite impure and mixed.

sentences.zh: 自西方之教，被於中國，去聖日遠，空門不行五濁，比丘但行粗法。

translations.literal: Since the teaching from the west spread in China, the days distant from the sages have grown long; the empty gate does not practice the five defilements, yet monks practice only coarse methods.
translations.idiomatic: Since the teaching from the west spread in China, the age has grown distant from the sages. The empty gate does not practice the five defilements, yet monks practice only coarse methods.

sentences.zh: 爰自後漢，至於陳、隋，僧之廢滅，其亦數乎！

translations.literal: From Later Han down to Chen and Sui, the abolition and destruction of monks—has this not happened several times!
translations.idiomatic: From Later Han down to Chen and Sui, the abolition and destruction of monks—has this not happened several times!

sentences.zh: 或至坑殺，殆無遺余。

translations.literal: At times they were buried alive or slaughtered, almost none remaining.
translations.idiomatic: At times they were buried alive or slaughtered, almost none remaining.

sentences.zh: 前代帝王，豈惡僧道之善如此之深耶？

translations.literal: Did emperors of former ages hate the goodness of monks and Daoists so deeply?
translations.idiomatic: Did emperors of former ages hate the goodness of monks and Daoists so deeply?

sentences.zh: 蓋其亂人亦已甚矣。

translations.literal: It is rather that their disordering of the people had already become extreme.
translations.idiomatic: It is rather that their disordering of the people had already become extreme.

sentences.zh: 且佛之立教，清凈無為，若以色見，即是邪法，開示悟入，唯有一門，所以三乘之人，比之外道。

translations.literal: Moreover, in establishing his teaching the Buddha was pure, quiet, and non-active; if one sees by form, that is heterodox law; to open, show, awaken, and enter there is only one gate—therefore those of the three vehicles are compared with outer ways.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in establishing his teaching the Buddha was pure, quiet, and non-active. To see by form is heterodox law. To open, show, awaken, and enter there is only one gate—therefore those of the three vehicles are compared with outer ways.

sentences.zh: 況今出家者皆是無識下劣之流，縱其戒行高潔，在於王者，已無用矣，況是茍避征徭，於殺盜淫，無所不犯者乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, those who leave home today are all ignorant and base streams; even if their precepts and conduct were lofty and pure, to a true king they would already be useless—not to mention those who evade corvée and tax and violate killing, theft, and lust without exception!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who leave home today are all ignorant and base. Even if their precepts and conduct were lofty and pure, to a true king they would already be useless—not to mention those who evade corvée and tax and violate killing, theft, and lust without exception!

sentences.zh: 今叔明之心甚善，然臣恐其奸吏詆欺，而去者未必非，留者不必是，無益於國，不能息奸。

translations.literal: Now Shuming's intent is very good, yet I fear that crafty clerks will slander and deceive; those who leave are not necessarily bad, and those who remain are not necessarily good—it benefits the state not and cannot still wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shuming's intent is very good, yet I fear crafty clerks will slander and deceive. Those who leave are not necessarily bad, and those who remain are not necessarily good. It benefits the state not and cannot still wickedness.

sentences.zh: 既不變人心，亦不因人心，強制力持，難致遠耳。

translations.literal: Since it neither transforms people's hearts nor follows people's hearts, forcibly compelling and rigidly maintaining it will be hard to reach far.
translations.idiomatic: Since it neither transforms people's hearts nor follows people's hearts, forcibly compelling and rigidly maintaining it will be hard to endure.

sentences.zh: 臣聞天生烝人，必將有職，遊行浮食，王制所禁。

translations.literal: I have heard that Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people and they must have duties; wandering about and eating without labor is forbidden by royal institutions.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people and they must have duties. Wandering about and eating without labor is forbidden by royal institutions.

sentences.zh: 故有才者受爵祿，不肖者出租征，此古之常道也。

translations.literal: Therefore the capable receive ranks and salary, the unworthy pay rent and tax—this is the constant way of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the capable receive ranks and salary, the unworthy pay rent and tax—this is the constant way of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今天下僧道，不耕而食，不織而衣，廣作危言險語，以惑愚者。

translations.literal: Now monks and Daoists throughout the realm eat without plowing and clothe themselves without weaving, widely making alarming words and dangerous speech to delude the foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Now monks and Daoists throughout the realm eat without plowing and clothe themselves without weaving, widely making alarming and dangerous speech to delude the foolish.

sentences.zh: 一僧衣食，歲計約三萬有余，五丁所出，不能致此。

translations.literal: One monk's food and clothing, reckoned yearly, comes to a little more than thirty thousand; what five households produce cannot reach this.
translations.idiomatic: One monk's food and clothing, reckoned yearly, comes to a little more than thirty thousand cash—more than five households can produce.

sentences.zh: 舉一僧以計天下，其費可知。

translations.literal: Take one monk to reckon the realm, and the expense can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolate from one monk to the whole realm, and the expense is plain.

sentences.zh: 陛下日旰憂勤，將去人害，此而不救，奚其為政？

translations.literal: Your Majesty toils in concern until sundown, intending to remove harm to the people—if this is not remedied, what is government for?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty toils in concern until sundown, intending to remove harm to the people. If this is not remedied, what is government for?

sentences.zh: 臣伏請僧道未滿五十者，每年輸絹四疋；

translations.literal: I humbly ask that monks and Daoists under fifty years of age pay four bolts of silk yearly;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that monks and Daoists under fifty years of age pay four bolts of silk yearly;

sentences.zh: 尼及女道士未滿五十者，每年輸絹二疋；

translations.literal: nuns and female Daoist priests under fifty pay two bolts of silk yearly;
translations.idiomatic: nuns and female Daoist priests under fifty pay two bolts of silk yearly;

sentences.zh: 其雜色役與百姓同。

translations.literal: their miscellaneous corvée duties are the same as commoners'.
translations.idiomatic: their miscellaneous corvée duties are the same as commoners'.

sentences.zh: 有才智者令入仕，請還俗為平人者聽。

translations.literal: Those with talent and wisdom are to be ordered into office; those who ask to return to lay life as ordinary people are to be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those with talent and wisdom are to be ordered into office. Those who ask to return to lay life as ordinary people are to be permitted.

sentences.zh: 但令就役輸課，為僧何傷。

translations.literal: Only let them perform corvée and pay dues—what harm is there in being monks?
translations.idiomatic: Only let them perform corvée and pay dues. What harm is there in remaining monks?

sentences.zh: 臣竊料其所出，不下今之租賦三分之一，然則陛下之國富矣，蒼生之害除矣。

translations.literal: I privately estimate that what they would pay would be no less than one third of present rent and tax; then Your Majesty's state would be rich and the harm to the common people removed.
translations.idiomatic: I estimate that what they would pay would amount to at least one third of present rent and tax. Your Majesty's treasury would grow rich and the harm to the common people would be removed.

sentences.zh: 其年過五十者，請皆免之。

translations.literal: Those over fifty years of age, I ask, should all be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Those over fifty years of age should all be exempted.

sentences.zh: 夫子曰：「五十而知天命。

translations.literal: The Master said: "At fifty one knows Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "At fifty one knows Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 」列子曰：「不班白，不知道。

translations.literal: Liezi said: "Without gray hair, one does not know the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Liezi said, "Without gray hair, one does not know the Way."

sentences.zh: 」人年五十，嗜欲巳衰，縱不出家，心已近道，況戒律檢其情性哉！

translations.literal: When a person is fifty, appetites and desires have already declined; even if he does not leave home, his heart is already near the Way—how much more when precepts restrain his disposition!
translations.idiomatic: At fifty, appetites and desires have already declined. Even if one does not leave home, the heart is already near the Way—how much more when precepts restrain one's disposition!

sentences.zh: 臣以為此令既行，僧道規避還俗者固已太半。

translations.literal: I believe that once this order is carried out, monks and Daoists who evade it by returning to lay life will already be more than half.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that once this order is carried out, more than half the monks and Daoists will evade it by returning to lay life.

sentences.zh: 其年老精修者，必盡為人師，則道、釋二教益重明矣。

translations.literal: Those who are old and finely cultivated will all become teachers of others, and then the two teachings of Daoism and Buddhism will grow still more weighty and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Those who are elderly and finely cultivated will all become teachers of others, and the two teachings of Daoism and Buddhism will grow still more weighty and clear.

sentences.zh: 議者是之，上頗善其言。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated approved it, and the emperor was quite pleased with his words.
translations.idiomatic: Those who deliberated approved it, and the emperor was quite pleased with his words.

sentences.zh: 大臣以二教行之已久，列聖奉之，不宜頓擾，宜去其太甚，其議不行。

translations.literal: Grandees held that the two teachings had long been practiced and successive sage emperors had honored them; they should not be suddenly disturbed—only their excesses removed—and the proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees held that the two teachings had long been practiced and successive sage emperors had honored them. They should not be suddenly disturbed—only their excesses removed—and the proposal was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 偃以才地當掌文誥，以躁求為時論所抑，郁郁不得誌。

translations.literal: Yan, by talent and position, ought to have managed literary edicts, but because of impatient striving was suppressed in contemporary opinion and brooded without fulfilling his ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: By talent and position Yan ought to have managed literary edicts, but impatient striving earned suppression in contemporary opinion, and he brooded without fulfilling his ambitions.

sentences.zh: 涇師之亂，從駕不及，匿於田家，為賊所得。

translations.literal: During the Jing troops' rebellion he could not keep up with the imperial train, hid in a farmer's household, and was seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jing troops' rebellion he could not keep up with the imperial train, hid in a farmer's household, and was seized by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 硃泚素知之，得偃甚喜，偽署中書舍人，僭號辭令，皆偃為之。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had long known him; when he obtained Yan he was greatly pleased, falsely appointed him Secretariat Drafter, and all usurpation proclamations and orders were written by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had long known him. When he obtained Yan he was greatly pleased, falsely appointed him Secretariat Drafter, and had Yan write all the usurpation proclamations and orders.

sentences.zh: 賊敗，與偽中丞崔宣、賊將杜如江、吳希光等十三人，李晟收之，俱斬於安國寺前。

translations.literal: When the rebels were defeated, together with the false Vice Censor Cui Xuan, rebel generals Du Rujiang, Wu Xiguang, and twelve others, he was taken by Li Sheng and all beheaded before Anguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were defeated, Yan was taken by Li Sheng together with the false Vice Censor Cui Xuan, rebel generals Du Rujiang, Wu Xiguang, and twelve others, and all were beheaded before Anguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：肇分陰陽，爰有生死，修短二事，賢愚一途。

translations.literal: The historian says: From the beginning yin and yang were divided, and thereby life and death arose; long life and short life are two affairs, yet worthy and foolish share one path.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: From the beginning yin and yang were divided, and thereby life and death arose. Long life and short life are two affairs, yet worthy and foolish share one path.

sentences.zh: 故君子遇夷險之機，不易其節；

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman, meeting occasions of peace or peril, does not alter his integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the gentleman, meeting occasions of peace or peril, does not alter his integrity;

sentences.zh: 小人昧逆順之道，而陷於刑。

translations.literal: the petty man, ignorant of the way of obedience and rebellion, falls into punishment.
translations.idiomatic: while the petty man, ignorant of the way of obedience and rebellion, falls into punishment.

sentences.zh: 鴻毛泰山，斯為至論。

translations.literal: A goose feather and Mount Tai—this is the supreme judgment.
translations.idiomatic: A goose feather weighed against Mount Tai—this is the supreme judgment.

sentences.zh: 令言遠總師徒，首為叛逆；

translations.literal: Lingyan from afar commanded master and troops and was first in rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Lingyan from afar commanded master and troops and was first in rebellion;

sentences.zh: 光晟初當委任，危輸款誠；

translations.literal: Guangcheng at first was entrusted with command and in peril offered sincere submission;
translations.idiomatic: Guangcheng at first was entrusted with command and in peril offered sincere submission;

sentences.zh: 源休雖曰士流，甚於元惡；

translations.literal: Yuan Xiu, though called a gentleman by birth, was worse than the chief villain;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiu, though called a gentleman by birth, was worse than the chief villain;

sentences.zh: 喬琳巧辭真主，俯就偽官；

translations.literal: Qiao Lin with clever words declined the true sovereign and stooped to false office;
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Lin with clever words declined the true sovereign and stooped to false office;

sentences.zh: 蔣鎮貪祿隳節，皆曰小人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhen clung to salary and destroyed his integrity—all are called petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhen clung to salary and destroyed his integrity—all are called petty men.

sentences.zh: 經綸之徒，不足言爾。

translations.literal: Men like Jinglun are not worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Jinglun are not worth speaking of.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：時爭逆順，命擊死生。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The age contends over obedience and rebellion; fate strikes at life and death.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The age contends over obedience and rebellion; fate strikes at life and death.

sentences.zh: 君子守節，小人正刑。

translations.literal: The gentleman keeps his integrity; the petty man receives correction by punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman keeps his integrity; the petty man receives correction by punishment.
